reasoning: The failing test `pages_create_new_page` assumes the nav's Pages bar is expanded by default and clicks `.nav-new-page` without ensuring it is visible. The application's actual default is the opposite: `get_show_pages_bar()` returns `setting is not None and setting.value == "true"`, so a fresh database with no `show_pages_bar` ApplicationSettings row renders `#navbar-pages-bar` with the `hidden` attribute; `nav.js` re-applies `bar.hidden` and `pages/nav.css` enforces `.navbar-pages-bar[hidden] { display: none; }`. The Pages toggle (`#nav-pages-toggle`) is a collapse/expand toggle, so clicking it is required to reveal `.nav-new-page` when the bar starts collapsed. Because the button is not actionable, the form POST never fires and `page.waitForURL(/\/pages\/\d+\/design$/)` times out. The server side is correct: `POST /pages` -> 302 `/pages/<id>` -> 302 `/pages/<id>/design` for a widget-less page, and the same spec goal is achievable once the bar is expanded (or via the direct `POST /pages` helper already present in the suite). The previous 6-test version of this suite passed because its sandbox happened to have the pages bar expanded; the new run against a fresh DB exposes the incorrect default-state assumption. `pages_presentation_view_renders_widgets` (which also clicks `.nav-page-tab`) is at risk for the same reason but was skipped in serial mode after the first failure.
suggestedAction: Before clicking `.nav-new-page`, ensure the Pages bar is expanded: if `#navbar-pages-bar` is hidden or `.nav-new-page` is not visible, click `#nav-pages-toggle` (and wait for the bar to become visible) first. Apply the same guard in `pages_presentation_view_renders_widgets` before clicking `.nav-page-tab`. Alternatively, use the existing direct `createPage`/`POST /pages` helper for creation scenarios that do not specifically need to exercise the nav control.
